definition: A term penalizing divergence between the trained policy and its reference model during RLHF, preventing the policy from wandering into degenerate high-reward but low-quality regions.
details: A term penalizing divergence between the trained policy and its reference model during RLHF, preventing the policy from wandering into degenerate high-reward but low-quality regions.

explainer.lead: A term in RLHF training that penalises divergence between the trained policy and its reference model. It stops the policy from drifting into high-reward but degenerate outputs.

tiers.eli5: It is a leash on the model, so it can learn to be more helpful without wandering off into weird behaviour just to game the score.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers add the penalty to the reward objective during reinforcement learning from human feedback, tuning its weight against reward gains. The pitfall is setting it too high, which freezes the policy near the reference model and blocks improvement.
tiers.paperLevel: A KL divergence term between the policy and its reference model added to the training objective, with a coefficient controlling its strength; it limits how far the policy can move, and the coefficient must be tuned.

explainer.example: During RLHF, a policy that starts producing repetitive text to exploit the reward model is pulled back by the KL term toward the reference model.
